units.title: Types, Causes & B12 vs Folate Stores
units.sec: Types, Causes & B12 vs Folate Stores
units.guide:
Macrocytic anemia (MCV >100 fL) divides into megaloblastic (lagging nuclear maturation) and normoblastic causes.
Megaloblastic causes include B12/folate/thiamine deficiency, DNA-synthesis inhibitors (cytarabine, hydroxyurea, 6-MP) and orotic aciduria.
B12 stores (2–5 mg; RDA 3–7 µg/d) last 2–5 years (>3 yr in vegetarians); folate stores (5–10 mg; RDA 50 µg/d) deplete in a few weeks.

units.title: Vitamin B12 Sources & Absorption
units.guide:
Dietary B12 (animal origin: adenosyl- and methylcobalamin) binds salivary R-factor/haptocorrin in the stomach.
Pancreatic enzymes split the complex in duodenum (parts 2 & 3) so B12 binds parietal-cell Intrinsic Factor (IF).
Ileal CUBAM receptors absorb IF-B12; plasma TC-2 forms holotranscobalamin for marrow RBC maturation.

units.title: B12 Deficiency, Transcobalamins & Roles
units.sec: Causes of B12 Deficiency, Transcobalamins & Functions
units.guide:
Causes: Pernicious anemia (most important), ileal disease (Crohn's, tropical sprue, TB), SIBO, TC-2/CUBAM defects (Imerslund–Gräsbeck), and D. latum.
Only B12, bile acids and Mg are absorbed solely in the ileum; TC-1 (from granulocytes) rises in MPN, while TC-2 mediates transport.
B12 is a cofactor for Homocysteine → Methionine and Methylmalonyl CoA → Succinyl CoA.

units.title: Folate Metabolism, Trap & Causes
units.sec: Folic Acid Metabolism, Folate Trap & Deficiency Causes
units.guide:
Folate is absorbed in proximal small bowel (jejunum/duodenum); dietary monoglutamate becomes circulating/storage 5-methyl THFA → THFA.
B12 deficiency causes the 'folate trap' (5-methyl THFA accumulation) and raises both homocysteine and methylmalonyl CoA (MMA is normal in pure folate deficiency).
Folate deficiency stems from ↓ intake (nutritional, major cause), celiac disease, ↑ demand (pregnancy, growth, hemolysis) and drugs (MTX, sulfasalazine, PPIs, pyrimethamine, triamterene, phenytoin).

units.title: Diagnosis of Megaloblastic Anemia
units.sec: Diagnosis of Megaloblastic Anemia & Bone Marrow
units.guide:
Serum B12 >300 pg is normal, <200 pg is deficient, and 200–300 pg prompts MMA, folate and homocysteine testing.
Smear shows megaloblasts, hypersegmented neutrophils (≥5 lobes, earliest change; <2 lobes = pseudo-Pelger–Huët in MDS), Cabot rings, basophilic stippling and Howell–Jolly bodies.
Pancytopenia occurs in 15–20% and warrants bone marrow smear (dyserythropoiesis, erythroid hyperplasia, ↓ M:E ratio, giant metamyelocytes).

units.title: Pernicious Anemia: Pathogenesis & Signs
units.guide:
Anti-parietal cell antibody is sensitive; anti-intrinsic factor antibody is specific; body involvement with antral sparing is classic.
Associated with Addison's disease, Type 1 DM and vitiligo; affects middle-aged to elderly females who are often asymptomatic.
Clinical features include lemon-yellow pallor (hemolytic jaundice), angular cheilitis, beefy-red atrophic glossitis and hyperpigmentation.

units.title: Pernicious Anemia: CNS, Workup & Rx
units.sec: Pernicious Anemia: CNS/GI Features, Workup & Treatment
units.guide:
SCD involves dorsal and lateral columns plus peripheral neuropathy and late cortical/optic changes (folate deficiency spares the spinal cord).
Increases risk of gastric carcinoid type 1 (m/c) and gastric adenocarcinoma (rare); workup shows oval macrocytosis, anti-IF Ab, ↑ gastrin and ↓↓ B12.
Hydroxycobalamin (1000 µg OD × 1 wk → weekly × 1 mo → monthly lifelong) raises reticulocytes by day 2–3 (peak day 6–8) and normalizes MCV in 10 weeks.
